page: Microsoft Azure E128ds_v7 is an Edsv7-family memory-optimized virtual machine utilizing the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 128 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 64 physical Intel Xeon 6973P-C cores on the x86_64 architecture, supporting two threads per core. The processor includes a 480 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1d cache, alongside hardware-accelerated instruction sets such as Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512) and Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX). The system is equipped with 1024.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 8.0 GB of RAM per vCPU, and includes 7559 GB of local storage with Premium Storage capabilities. No GPUs are present on this instance.

Benchmark data shows a clear distinction between single-core and multi-core performance. While single-core stress-ng CPU performance and PassMark memory scores fall within the average tier (middle 50%), multi-core metrics are highly competitive. The instance achieves top-tier (top 10%) results in multi-core stress-ng CPU performance, PassMark CPU score, and PassMark database operations. Memory bandwidth is exceptionally high, with uncached read-only large block speeds reaching 655.3 GB/sec and cached small block read speeds at 10642.11 GB/sec, both placing in the top 10%. Redis SET operations also perform in the top tier, registering 209.67 million operations per second.

The qualitative cost efficiency of the E128ds_v7 is defined by its high memory-to-vCPU ratio and massive local storage capacity, making it a resource-dense option for memory-bound workloads. However, workloads dependent on single-threaded execution or raw memory latency may experience average performance, as reflected in the middle-tier single-core benchmarks and LLM text generation speeds (which average 4.6 to 91.81 tokens/sec depending on model size). Conversely, prompt processing for LLM inference is strong, placing in the top 25%. This hardware profile is suited for large-scale database operations, memory-intensive enterprise applications, multi-threaded data decompression, and caching layers like Redis.
